standard.title: Vocabulary in familiar contexts
standard.description: recognise and develop awareness of vocabulary used in familiar contexts related to everyday experiences, personal interests and topics taught at school
standard.prior_knowledge: Students bring oral vocabulary from home and community contexts. They have not yet been asked to consciously attend to vocabulary — to notice, collect and develop awareness of words in relation to specific topics and contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can recognise and use vocabulary relevant to everyday experiences, personal interests and school topics — drawing on multiple sources to expand their word knowledge and applying vocabulary in both imaginative and informative contexts.

nodes.label: Topics have words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify that topics and contexts have specific vocabulary — particular words that go with particular subjects or activities.
nodes.minimum_width: Name at least three words that belong to one familiar topic (e.g. words related to families, or words used in a current class topic).
nodes.typical_width: Identify and collect vocabulary associated with school topics; recognise learning area–specific words across multiple topics; notice when new words are introduced.
wider: Build a word wall for a current topic and continue adding to it as new vocabulary is encountered across the unit
Compare the vocabulary of two different topics — what words appear in both? What words are unique to each?

response_modes.reason: Vocabulary acquisition at Foundation is fundamentally about accumulation — students need to encounter and retain many words across many contexts before vocabulary awareness becomes a generative habit.

success_criteria: Student can name at least three words associated with a familiar topic.
Student can identify a word as a 'topic word' when it is introduced in a new context.

nodes.label: Vocabulary grows through experience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify multiple ways of encountering and learning new vocabulary — through interactions, texts, images, objects and play.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one new word encountered in class and explain where or how they came across it.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise that vocabulary can be expanded through informal interactions, planned experiences, texts, images, artefacts and objects; draw on vocabulary encountered in multiple ways — including imaginative play — to use words in context.
wider: Investigate how role-play activities generate new vocabulary — comparing words used in different dramatic contexts (shopkeeper, scientist, storyteller)
Explore vocabulary from different cultural contexts in the class — including words from First Nations Australian languages or other community languages
Compare vocabulary encountered through visual texts (picture books, films) with vocabulary encountered through oral interaction and real objects

response_modes.reason: Students may think vocabulary grows only through 'word learning lessons'. Multiple sources — play, objects, images, community language — help build the broader understanding that vocabulary is encountered everywhere.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The cross-curricular vocabulary dimension — and especially the opportunity to explore First Nations Australian language words and diverse community languages alongside English — offers rich and culturally significant vocabulary experiences beyond what is strictly required.
success_criteria: Student can identify at least two different ways they have encountered new vocabulary.
Student can use a recently acquired vocabulary word appropriately in speech or in a text they are creating.
